claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post.
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
Jev's decision-making primitives are confidence scoring, multiple choice, and yes/no (noul) questions.
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes.
GeoDeploy uses great-circle distance as a coverage measure.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog.
GeoDeploy's module registry includes EKS, AKS, GKE; ECR, ACR, Artifact Registry; DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare.
GeoDeploy uses the Pulumi Automation API to run a preview then an update, with one stack per region, and won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes plan.json and plan.md.
Jev provides choice(), score(), and noul() primitives; choice returns the pick, a probability distribution, and a confidence; noul answers yes/no with a single probability.
Jev only selects from closed sets, so a hallucinated region or made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.
GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates per geo.
The @typesafe-ai/sdk package exports choice, noul, and score.
The TypeSafeClient has a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers.
GeoDeploy ranking weight profiles are latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.
GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95, new-cluster region 0.90, existing-stack region 0.75, ingress/autoscaling module 0.85, node-pool tier 0.60, global floor 0.50.
GeoDeploy falls back to a deterministic price comparison when a gate fails, the API errors or times out, or upstream is unreachable, and `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

In self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), above 0.85 confidence resizes apply automatically, between 0.70 and 0.85 are suggested for human approval, and below 0.70 fall back to a deterministic rule.
CPU utilization alone is a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with other signals.
TypeSafe advises to "describe situations, not degrees" when writing rubrics.
The GitHub repository pulumi/devx-geodeploy exists and is open source.
